description: Item/inventory table investigation results. Static analysis could not locate a dedicated item table. This game appears to be a tactical RPG (SRPG) where items may be replaced by skill/technique systems, or item data is accessed through indirection that requires dynamic analysis.

skill_table.description: Skill/technique definitions that may serve as the item system in this tactical RPG

character_stat_table.description: Character stat definitions that may include equipment modifiers

level_up_table.description: Level-up stat progression (confirmed separate from items)

possible_explanations: Items are embedded in the battle config or skill system rather than a standalone table
Item names are not stored as SJIS text (may use a custom encoding)
Item data is accessed through a chain of indirect pointers requiring runtime tracing
This SRPG uses a technique/scroll system instead of traditional consumable items
Item effects are code-driven (implemented in function calls rather than data tables)
recommended_next_steps: Use mGBA Qt frontend with Lua scripting to open the in-game menu
Dump WRAM before and after acquiring an item
Diff WRAM to identify item record array in runtime memory
Use LLDB watchpoints on suspected WRAM addresses during menu interaction
notes: All 6 candidate addresses from prior analysis were examined for SJIS item names. No clear item name text was found near any candidate. The ROM contains many instances of the SJIS character 薬 (medicine) but in unrelated data. The skill table at 0x546100 with 12 entries of 16 bytes remains the most likely item-adjacent structure. In this Naruto tactical RPG, 'items' may be ninja techniques/scrolls managed through the skill system rather than a traditional RPG inventory.
